- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, especially if recent price action is trending up.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), particularly if recent price has been consolidating or declining.
- Avoid sharp upward spikes in forecast after recent price peaks — model tends to overreact and overshoot, especially if sentiment is positive but recent price is flat or slightly down.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, model often lags in adjusting downward — delay correction by 1–2 periods.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model tends to overestimate volatility in early periods — smooth out early forecast peaks if sentiment is weak or neutral.
- If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over last 5 days, model should not forecast sharp declines — avoid “sudden drop” patterns unless sentiment turns negative.
- If true outcome is significantly below forecast (e.g., >10% gap), check if sentiment was bullish 3–5 days prior — if yes, reduce forecast by 5–15% to account for mean reversion or sentiment decay.
